fields.title: Downtown Enhanced Services
fields.intent: The City of Flagstaff seeks proposals from qualified contractors to establish a term contract for Enhanced Services (sanitation, maintenance, beautification, snow/cinder removal, and programming) in Historic Downtown Flagstaff.
fields.scope: Enhanced services within Downtown Flagstaff on City property, public rights-of-way and Heritage Square, including sanitation (graffiti removal, excrement removal, pressure washing/surface cleaning, parking kiosk exterior cleaning, weed removal, restroom cleaning and servicing, waste container servicing, painting red and yellow curbs), snow and cinder removal, post-special-event cleanup, and dedicated programs (Clean Team Ambassador Program, Paint Downtown Green Program, and enhanced event programming of at least three free public events per week on average). Contractor may provide the services directly or subcontract them under its management.
fields.submissionDeadline: Friday, October 31, 2025, at 3:00 PM Arizona Time
fields.questionsDeadline: Friday, October 24, 2025, at 5:00 pm Arizona time
fields.eligibleApplicants: Qualified contractors legally qualified to contract with the City and holding any required active State of Arizona license(s); subcontracting is permitted.
fields.submissionMethod: Electronic submission only, via the PlanetBids online bid platform (https://www.planetbids.com/portal/portal.cfm?CompanyID=27606) prior to the Closing Date and Time; no hard copies.
fields.evaluationCriteria: Scored by an Evaluation Committee: Proposer Qualifications, Experience and Expertise 35%; Presented approach 30%; Proposed Fee 25%; Sustainability 10% (total 100%). Responsibility factors are also considered, and the Committee may short list proposers, hold discussions/presentations, and request "Best and Final" offers.

fields.title: Sidewalk, Road, Bridge, and Drainage Construction (Blanket Contract 2026)
fields.issuer: City of Providence, Rhode Island — Board of Contract and Supply; issuing department: Department of Public Works
fields.issuerContact: Bryant Anderson, Deputy Chief Engineer, Engineering Division, Department of Public Works (technical/specification questions); Grace Diaz, MBE/WBE Outreach Director (MBE/WBE forms); Purchasing Department (process questions)
fields.intent: The City of Providence Department of Public Works seeks to qualify multiple contractors under a blanket contract to perform sidewalk, road, bridge, drainage and other similar construction within the public right-of-way or other City-owned areas as funding opportunities and needs arise, with work assigned by Task Order.
fields.scope: Work is divided into two categories: 1) Sidewalk, Road, and Drainage Construction — full frontage sidewalk repairs, spot sidewalk repairs, utility patch restorations (road and sidewalk), full depth road restoration including granular and rigid base, minor milling/paving, drainage work including catch basin/manhole repairs, installation of speed lumps/raised crosswalks; and 2) Bridge Construction — bridge construction, maintenance and repairs. Also includes restoration of roadway striping and traffic detection loops and all incidentals.
fields.submissionDeadline: Monday, March 9, 2026 at 2:15 P.M. (bids publicly opened at 2:15 P.M.)
fields.contractTerm: Runs through December 31, 2027, with three (3) one-year renewal options (1/1/2028–12/31/2028, 1/1/2029–12/31/2029, and 1/1/2030–12/31/2030), exercisable upon mutual agreement of the parties.
fields.eligibleApplicants: Qualified and responsible contractors with at least 5 years construction experience within the last 7 years on Roadway and/or Bridge Improvement Projects; out-of-state corporations must be registered to transact business in Rhode Island. MBE/WBE participation goals (20% combined) apply to Task Orders, and MBE/WBE firms are actively sought.
fields.submissionMethod: Physical delivery of sealed bids to the Department of the City Clerk, City Hall Room 311, 25 Dorrance Street, Providence, RI 02903 — 2 copies (one original and one paper copy) in sealed, labeled envelopes plus an electronic copy in .PDF format on a USB flash drive. No CDs or emailed PDFs accepted.
fields.evaluationCriteria: Award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder(s) meeting RFP requirements; the City qualifies multiple responsive, qualified and experienced contractors. Bidders' qualifications (5 years' experience, equipment, personnel, financials, references) are investigated; a Pre-Bid Award Descope Meeting may be required. For projects with items on the Schedule of Unit Prices, DPW estimates project costs from submitted unit prices to determine the lowest bidder, but timeliness to schedule or complete the work is also a consideration, and the City reserves the right to award to any Contractor if in the City's best interest.
fields.terminationConditions: The City may terminate upon five (5) days' written notice if the contractor fails to observe any terms and conditions or if the City believes the contractor's ability to perform has been materially impaired (e.g., loss of insurance coverage, lapsing of surety bond, bankruptcy, appointment of a receiver); upon termination the contractor is entitled to just and equitable compensation for satisfactory work completed. Under the General Conditions, if the Contractor or a Subcontractor refuses or fails to prosecute the work with diligence to ensure completion within the specified time, or violates any other provision, the Owner may by written notice terminate the Contractor's right to proceed, take over and complete the work, and hold the Contractor and sureties liable for additional costs and liquidated damages. Failure to comply with insurance requirements is a material breach entitling the Owner to terminate or suspend immediately. Noncompliance with Section 3 / equal opportunity requirements may result in cancellation, termination or suspension.

DKC44-80RIB: Strong performance across all yield zones tested; great ear flex to compensate in lower plant populations; excellent emergence and seedling vigour; plant at medium populations for best results; performs best on clay and loam soil types; excellent drydown.

Think Before You Bin Run considerations

Verification Required — the last patent on the original Roundup Ready® soybean trait expired a few years ago and U.S. farmers may legally plant saved seed from some Roundup Ready® varieties, but check with your seed supplier whether a specific variety is covered by other intellectual property rights and the seed-saving policy. Higher Seeding Rate — a higher seeding rate may be required for bin-run Roundup Ready® soybeans compared to new branded seed. Yield Loss — Roundup Ready 2 Yield®, Roundup Ready 2 Xtend® and XtendFlex® varieties typically have higher yield opportunity than Roundup Ready® varieties. Cleanout Loss — loss of seed and/or shrink occurs during seed cleaning and handling of bin-run seed. Seed Treatment Costs — treating seed adds the cost of the treatment and its application. Lost Income — every bushel of saved seed planted is a bushel not sold as commodity grain. Increased Seed Management — saving bin-run seed requires managing harvest operations and grain storage so seed isn't co-mingled with seed covered by intellectual property rights. Contacts for seed IP questions or anonymous saved seed tips: call 1-866-99-BAYER; write Trait Stewardship, 622 Emerson Road, Suite 150, Creve Coeur, MO 63141; or submit a request at cropscience.bayer.us/contact.
